new_finding_p0.blocking_scope: V2_SSOT_FROZEN (via rc-6-r1's exclusion validity) and all future ACCEPTED_BOUNDED_RESIDUAL_RISK grants
new_finding_p0.pre_existing_since: V2-C005/C006 era (the top-level accepted_by_audit_sha/accepted_by_audit_branch/accepted_by_audit_report validation block in residual_in_force(), NOT touched by V2-C012's H-1..H-5 rewrite)
new_finding_p0.statement: residual_in_force()'s TOP-LEVEL grant-evidence check (accepted_by_audit_sha/accepted_by_audit_branch/accepted_by_audit_report -- distinct from V2-C012's NEW per-condition audit_sha check, H-3) verifies only (a) 40-hex format, (b) that `git show <sha>:<report_path>` succeeds, (c) that the resulting JSON's id/verdict/new_class fields match. It never calls merge-base --is-ancestor (or anything equivalent) to confirm the sha is actually reachable from the declared audit branch. Since `git show` succeeds for ANY commit object present in the local repository regardless of ref reachability, and promote_landing_main.sh:91 hardcodes REPO=/home/sieg/projects-wsl/ProjectFinal (the SAME shared .git object store used by every worktree under this project, per CLAUDE.md's worktree-sharing convention), any agent with ordinary local git write access (i.e. every role: exec, control, adversarial, ssot, shadow-lane agents) can fabricate a dangling, never-pushed commit containing a spoofed audit-report JSON and have it accepted as legitimate grant evidence.
new_finding_p0.self_correction: My own V2-C011 §5.4 H-3 row claimed the top-level accepted_by_audit_sha check 'does all four things' including '감사 브랜치 확인' (branch/ancestor verification). That claim was FALSE -- I did not verify it empirically at the time. control's H-3 commit message explicitly benchmarks the new per-condition check against 'the same strength as [AUDIT_ANCESTRY]/accepted_by_audit_sha', i.e. control built H-3 assuming the top-level mechanism already had ancestor verification (trusting my incorrect V2-C011 description), and correctly replicated 40-hex/commit-resolve/report-content checks for the new per-condition field -- but never revisited the pre-existing top-level field to see whether it, too, needed the ancestor check it was credited with already having. I correct that overclaim here.

live_exploit_3_combined_with_L2.description: Full end-to-end self-approval bypass: fabricate a brand-new _ABRR_CANON entry (simulating control's own canon-editing capability, L-2's scenario) for a wholly invented finding id, register a new orchestrator_registered.findings entry for that id with the dangling-commit grant as top-level evidence, reuse REAL ancestor-valid evidence for the one per-condition requirement (C-1, genuinely satisfied, to pass H-3 honestly), and keep the visibility bookkeeping (accepted_bounded_residual_risk counter, accepted_residual_ids) self-consistent -- exactly what a competent attacker would do.

A wholly fabricated finding, with a wholly fabricated audit verdict that no real adversarial or ssot lane ever wrote, was accepted as a legitimate ACCEPTED_BOUNDED_RESIDUAL_RISK exclusion and would silently keep the ledger's own internal counters consistent.
live_exploit_3_combined_with_L2.significance: This directly answers the orchestrator's question about whether L-2 (canon self-editability) is a real hole: L-2 ALONE is not exploitable (control's reasoning that 'a real grant is still required' is correct in isolation) -- but L-2 COMBINED with this P0 constitutes a complete, working self-approval bypass of the entire ACCEPTED_BOUNDED_RESIDUAL_RISK safety mechanism.

L-1.control_claim: condition-evidence check scans ALL audit-report JSONs in the audit_sha commit's tree and accepts if ANY affirms the id; an OLDER report in the same tree negating it does not veto.
L-1.verdict: Accurately disclosed. No live exploit path found against the CURRENT real conditions (C-1/C-2/C-5-1) -- their current audit_sha values (0dfb6d5/56f69f3/30093b4) are the genuine, non-superseded, non-contradicted verdicts. Left as a theoretical residual, not escalated to a finding: exploiting it would require an actual historical case of a stale/retracted affirmative verdict for one of the three gate-required conditions, which does not currently exist in this project's history.

L-2.control_claim: _ABRR_CANON lives in the script, which control can edit; new grants still require a real ACCEPT_RECLASSIFY verdict, so this is 'intended friction', not a hole.
L-2.verdict: Standalone claim is textually accurate. However its safety argument depends entirely on 'a real ACCEPT_RECLASSIFY verdict' being unforgeable -- and §new_finding_p0 shows it is forgeable. live_exploit_3_combined_with_L2 demonstrates the combination working end to end. Judgment: L-2 is a real hole once combined with the P0 above; not a hole in isolation.

p2_new.statement: A2 §1.13's new dom_order uniqueness constraint says 'unique within (observation_id, document)' and adds an 'iframe boundary' paragraph, but no column named document/document_id/frame_id/frame_url exists anywhere in fact_primary_action_candidate's A1 §5.1 column table, nor anywhere else in the entire 00~02 pack. p2_new.why_it_matters: The uniqueness constraint, as literally written, is not checkable against the actual schema: there is no stored field to key the constraint on, and selector alone does not disambiguate documents (two candidates in different iframes could share an identical selector string).
p2_new.remediation_minimal: Add a document-scope column (e.g. document_index or frame_id, 0-based, 0=top document) to A1 §5.1's column table and point A2 §1.13's uniqueness constraint at it, OR explicitly scope the current spec to single-document pages and narrow the uniqueness constraint to (observation_id) alone until iframe support is designed.
